standard_prerequisites.name: Perfectness of complexes is a local property
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Stacks Project, Cohomology of Sheaves, section on perfect complexes (locality of perfect objects)
standard_prerequisites.use: Justifies reducing the perfectness check on X to the open covering by U and V.

core_obligations: Reduce to a local check: perfectness is local on X, so it suffices to verify Rj_*E on the two open pieces U and V = X \ j(T) (proof lines 12707-12708).
Compute the restrictions: Rj_*E|_U = E, which is perfect by hypothesis on E, and Rj_*E|_V = 0, because E vanishes on U \ T (proof lines 12709-12710).
proof_roadmap: Use locality of perfectness to reduce to an open cover.
Cover X by U and V = X \ j(T).
Check perfectness on U (it is E) and on V (it is zero).
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for an open immersion j : U -> X, the pushforward Rj_*E of a perfect complex E on U is perfect on X whenever the cohomology sheaves of E are supported on a closed subset T with j(T) closed in X. The proof rests on locality of perfectness, splits the check into the two-part open cover U, V = X \ j(T), and uses that Rj_*E restricts to E on U and vanishes on V because E vanishes on U \ T (proof lines 12707-12710). H2: the support hypothesis is what makes V open and the vanishing on V valid; identifying that is the non-routine step.
